review: The hymn is Romans 8:31–39: 1:1–1:3 quotes מִי יַפְרִידֵנוּ / מִי יִשְׁטֹן (v35, v33), 2:1–2:2 the 'no condemnation' of v1, and 6:4 the conqueror of v37.
4:3 לְהַפְחִידֵנִי אָנִי — 'to frighten me — I am…'; the Arabic فَأَنَا ('so I am') begins the answer in the next line; Hebrew keeps אָנִי at the end of the line so the caesura falls as in the print.
5:1 גְּדוּדֵיהֶם — the glossary fixes גְּדוּד for جُنْد; the suffix makes it 'their troops' without an extra word.
5:4 שֶׂה בְּלִי רֹעֶה — 'a sheep without a shepherd' (Num 27:17, Matt 9:36); the Arabic شَاةٌ بِلَا رَاعِي is that image and the Hebrew is the fixed phrase.
7:1 כְלִי־נֶשֶׁק שָׁלֵם — 'full armor' (Eph 6:11, כְּלִי נֶשֶׁק); the construct is the biblical term for weapons, not a modern collective.
